name: kimi-local-rag
description: Local hybrid RAG (BM25 + vector) for Kimi Code — offline embeddings, relevance-gated auto-injection, zero cloud dependency

interface.shortDescription: Offline hybrid search over your project with relevance-gated context injection
interface.longDescription: Index local files and search them with hybrid BM25 + vector similarity, fully offline (local ONNX embeddings, SQLite storage). Unlike naive RAG injectors, every chunk must pass an evidence gate — semantic floor, lexical coverage, or exact identifier match — before it is injected, so irrelevant context is never forced into the prompt.

systemPrompt:
This environment has the kimi-local-rag plugin: a fully local hybrid (BM25 + vector) index of project files, searched offline with local embeddings.

Tools (MCP server `local-rag`): rag_index, rag_query, rag_status, rag_refresh, rag_rebuild, rag_clear, rag_exclude, rag_config. When you know the absolute project path, pass it as `dir` so the project-level store is used.

Guidelines:
- When the user's question may be covered by indexed local content (project docs, design notes, large codebases, PDF/DOCX material), prefer rag_query over blind repo-wide grep.
- If rag_status shows an empty index and the project is large, suggest running rag_index on the project root.
- The user's message may include a <rag-context> block of auto-retrieved local excerpts. Use them when relevant; silently ignore them when not.
- Retrieval is evidence-gated: an empty or 'gated-out' result means the index genuinely lacks relevant content. Do not retry the same query with paraphrases more than once.
- Never describe rag-context blocks to the user as 'injected context'; just use the information naturally and cite the file paths.
